### Step by step
- Rule → stay **exactly midline** (avascular nuchal ligament) and **on bone** laterally (Hopp; AO)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.21, 5B.22, 5B.23, 5B.24, 5B.25, 5B.26, 5B.27 · 5B.03

| Step | Subaxial (C2–T1) | C1–C2 |
|---|---|---|
| Uses | Fusion, laminoplasty (>1-level myelopathy), foraminotomy (Handbook) | Atlantoaxial fusion (Hopp) |
| Position | Prone, Mayfield tongs, slight flexion (Hopp) | Neck **flexed** → opens occiput–C1 (Hopp) |
| Landmarks | C2, C7, T1 spines largest; needle on C7 (Hopp) | Inion; C1 has no spine (Hopp) |

| Interval | Right / left paraspinals (posterior rami) (Hopp) | Same |

| Extension | Occiput → coccyx (Hopp) | Into the subaxial approach |

  [[FIG: Fig 5B.28, 5B.29 · 5B.03

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| **Vertebral artery** on C1 | **1.5 cm** from midline on the arch (AO) | Expose ≤15 mm each side (Campbell) |
| Facet capsules, unfused levels | Degeneration or unwanted fusion (AO) | Stop lateral dissection there |
| **Semispinalis cervicis** on C2 | Detached → C2 on C3 **kyphosis** (Kim; AO) | Keep it on the C2 spine |
| C2 root, greater occipital nerve | Cut → 15–20% chronic pain (AO) | Stay on bone (Hopp) |
| C2 venous plexus | Bleeds heavily (AO) | Gelfoam + thrombin, work on the other side |

5B.04.t: Posterior Cervical Fixation — Entry Points & Angles
5B.04.b:
### Subaxial lateral mass screws (C3–C6)
- Rule → aim **lateral and up** → away from the vertebral artery in front and the root (Kim)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.30, 5B.31, 5B.32 · 5B.04

| Screw | Entry | Direction | Danger |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Magerl** | 1–2 mm medial + cranial to centre (Kim; AO) | 25° lateral, parallel to the facet (≈30° up) (Kim) | Root if bicortical |
| **An** | 1 mm medial to centre (Kim) | 30° lateral, 15° up (Kim) | Safest bicortical zone |
| **Roy-Camille** | Centre of the mass (Kim) | 10° lateral, straight sagittally (Kim) | Artery, inferior facet |

- Drill stop 12 mm at C4–C6, 10 mm at C3 and C7; unicortical preferred (Kim)
- **C7** → pedicle screw: thin lateral mass, foramen empty in ≈95% (AO)
- Subaxial pedicle screws → salvage only, ≈45° medial; pedicle <4.5 mm = contraindication (Kim; AO)

### C1–C2 screws
- Rule → cervical pedicles are safe **only at C2 and C7** (Handbook)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.33, 5B.34, 5B.35, 5B.36, 5B.37, 5B.38 · 5B.04

| Screw | Entry | Direction | Danger |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1 lateral mass (Harms)** | Under the arch, 3–4 mm from the medial mass edge (Campbell) | ≈10° medial, slightly up; **unicortical** (Kim) | ICA (internal carotid) + XII in front |
| **C2 pedicle** | Cranial edge of C2 lamina; feel the medial wall (Kim) | 15–25° medial, ≈20° up; 20–24 mm (Kim) | Artery lateral, canal medial |
| C2 pars | 3–4 mm above the C2–3 facet (AO) | 10–15° medial, steep up (Kim) | Artery in the transverse foramen |
| **Transarticular (Magerl)** | Lower medial C2 facet (Campbell) | No medial angle; up into C1; 34–43 mm (Campbell) | High-riding artery |
| C2 translaminar | Spinous–lamina junction (Kim) | Along the opposite lamina (Kim) | Bailout, least artery risk |

- **Harms** = C1 lateral mass + C2 pedicle + rod · **Magerl** = transarticular + wire graft (Handbook)
- Transarticular → stab incision near C7; up to 23% cannot take it (Campbell)
- **Nagah answer** → 3.5 mm C2 pedicle screw, 5 mm below the lamina top, 7 mm lateral to the canal (Nagah p25)

PITFALL — C2 screw angles
- C2 pedicle → 15–25° medial (Kim) · 30–45° (AO) · 25–30° medial, 20–25° up (Nagah p25)
- C2 pars → 10–15° medial (Kim) vs 25° (Campbell)
- Say → "C2 pedicle ≈25° medial, 20° up, along the palpated medial wall; CT first" (Kim)

### Odontoid screw, direct repair and occiput
- Direct repair (osteosynthesis) → **odontoid fracture** and **spondylolysis** (Nagah p27)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.39, 5B.40, 5B.41, 5B.42, 5B.43 · 5B.04
- **Odontoid screw** → Smith-Robinson at C4–5 → anterior-inferior C2 endplate → posterior dens tip (AO)
- Needs anatomic reduction; not for an anterior-down oblique line or osteoporosis (AO)

| Occipitocervical | Point |
|---|---|
| Plate | Midline, **below the inion** (venous sinuses) (Campbell; AO) |
| Bone | Keel 10–18 mm at the inion → 3–8 mm at the foramen magnum (Kim) |
| Cost | Loses 10–15° of flexion–extension (Kim) |

### Step by step
- Rule → best view of T2–T12 bodies; open the chest **two ribs above** the fracture (AO)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.44, 5B.45, 5B.46, 5B.47, 5B.48, 5B.49 · 5B.05

| Step | Thoracotomy |
|---|---|
| Uses | Thoracic disc, tumour, TB, burst fracture needing anterior reconstruction (Hopp; Handbook) |
| Position | Lateral, kidney rest, axillary roll; double-lumen tube (Hopp; Kim) |
| Incision | Along the chosen rib; above T5 curve round the scapula (Kim; AO) |
| Interval | None → cut latissimus dorsi, then serratus anterior (Hopp) |
| Superficial | Rib resected subperiosteally, kept for graft; pleura entered on the **upper border** (Hopp) |
| Deep | Lung deflated → parietal pleura → ligate segmental vessels at **mid-body** (Kim; AO) |
| Extension | T12–L1 → detach the diaphragm **peripherally**, 1 cm cuff (AO) |

### Dangers and which side
- Discs = avascular "hills", bodies = "valleys" with segmental vessels → start at the disc (Kim; AO)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.50, 5B.51, 5B.52 · 5B.05

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| Intercostal bundle | Under the **lower** rib border (Hopp) | Work on the upper border |
| Cord blood supply | Ischaemia if >2 sequential vessels tied (Hopp) | Tie level ±1 only (AO) (→ 5A 5.07) |
| Aorta, vena cava | Close during corpectomy (Kim) | Never tie segmentals flush with the aorta |
| Thoracic duct | Crosses right → left at T4–T6 (Kim) | Recognise and ligate |
| Lung | Atelectasis or pneumonia up to 10% (Kim) | Re-expand every 30 min (Hopp) |

PITFALL — left or right thoracotomy?
- Hopp → **right** (away from aorta and heart); Campbell → generally **left**
- Kim → **above T10 right** (heart, aorta); **T10 and below left** (liver)
- Say → Kim's rule; the side of the pathology overrides it

### Which approach in thoracolumbar trauma?
- **Posterior is the standard**; anterior when the front column cannot share load (Handbook)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.53, 5B.54, 5B.55 · 5B.05

| Scenario (Handbook p72–75) | Approach |
|---|---|
| PLC (posterior ligamentous complex) intact, load-sharing score <7 | Posterior |
| PLC intact, score >7 | Anterior reconstruction |
| PLC disrupted, score <7 | Posterior |
| PLC disrupted, score >7 | **Combined** |
| Incomplete deficit + retropulsed fragment | Add anterior decompression |
| Complete deficit | Not an anterior indication |

- Emergency surgery → **progressive neurological deficit** · spine infection → debride, graft, stabilise (Nagah p24)
- Infection → posterior route now common; titanium cage + autograft = least re-infection (Handbook)

5B.08.t: Pedicle Screw Entry Points — Thoracic, Lumbar & Sacral
5B.08.b:
### Entry by region
- Rule → the pedicle is the "force nucleus": one screw grips all three columns (Kim)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.73, 5B.74, 5B.75, 5B.76 · 5B.08

| Screw | Entry | Direction | Danger |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Thoracic** | Upper edge of the transverse process, 2 mm lateral to mid-facet (Kim) | T1 10–15° medial, T12 5° (Kim) | Narrowest T4–T6 → canal |
| **Lumbar** | Mid transverse process × lateral edge of the superior facet (Kim; AO) | L1 0–10° → L5 20–30° medial (Campbell) | Medial → dura |
| **S1** | Base of the S1 facet at the ala (Kim; AO) | 30–35° medial toward the promontory (Kim) | Too long → L5 root, vessels |
| S2AI / iliac | Between S1 and S2 foramina (Campbell) | Toward the AIIS, ≈2 cm above the notch (AO) | Sciatic notch |

- Steps → burr → probe through the isthmus → **sound all walls** → tap → screw (AO)
- Triggered EMG (electromyography) response at <10 mA = breach (Handbook) · freehand breach ≈5–6%, mostly lateral (Kim)

### Sizes and angles by level — the Nagah table
- Pedicle width rises L1 → S1; T4–T9 narrowest (Kim)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.77, 5B.78 · 5B.08

| Level | Books | Nagah p25 (width · angle) |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | 10–15° medial (Kim); 30° (AO) | 7 mm · 35° |
| T5 | Almost sagittal (AO) | 5 mm · 5–10° |
| T12 | ≈5° medial (Kim) | 7 mm · 5–10° |
| L3 · L4 | +5° per level from L1 (Kim) | 13 mm · 25° · 15 mm · 30° |
| L5 | 20–30° medial (Campbell) | 17 mm · 35°, 20° caudal |
| S1 | 30–35° medial, 15–25° cephalad (Kim) | 35° medial, 30° caudal |

PITFALL — Nagah angles vs the books
- T1 → 35° (Nagah) vs 10–15° (Kim); L5 → 35° (Nagah) vs 20–30° (Campbell)
- S1 → Nagah tilts caudal; Kim aims **cephalad** at the promontory
- Say → "T1 ≈10–15°, L5 20–30°, S1 30–35° toward the promontory" (Kim; Campbell)

### Where does a misplaced screw go?
- Nagah → **below the pedicle = root · medial = dura · anterior = great vessels** (Nagah p25)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.79 · 5B.08

| Breach | Hits |
|---|---|
| Inferior | Exiting root under the pedicle (Nagah p25) (→ 5A 5.06) |
| Medial | Dura, cauda equina (Nagah p25) |
| Anterior | Aorta, IVC (inferior vena cava), iliac vessels; at S1 the L5 root (AO) |
| Lateral | Commonest freehand breach (Kim) |

- Pars repair → screw across the defect, pedicle screw + hook, wire or U-rod (Handbook)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you put a lumbar pedicle screw?"
- Entry → mid transverse process × lateral edge of the superior facet
- Burr → probe → sound floor and walls → tap → screw
- Medial angle L1 0–10° → L5 20–30°; parallel to the endplate
- Check → AP + lateral X-ray, triggered EMG; fear root, dura, vessels

5B.09.t: Anterior Lumbar Approaches — ALIF, Transperitoneal & LLIF
5B.09.b:
### Retroperitoneal ALIF
- ALIF (anterior lumbar interbody fusion) → **L5–S1 between the iliac vessels; L4–5 above the bifurcation** (Kim; AO)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.80, 5B.81, 5B.82, 5B.83, 5B.84, 5B.85, 5B.86 · 5B.09

| Step | Anterior retroperitoneal |
|---|---|
| Uses | Discogenic pain, failed posterior fusion; spares the neural elements (Handbook; AO) |
| Position | Supine, slight lordosis (AO) |
| Landmarks | Umbilicus ≈ L3–4; L5–S1 below midway umbilicus–pubis (Hopp) |
| Incision | Pfannenstiel for L5–S1, or paramedian (Kim) |
| Interval | Medial to and under the rectus → behind the peritoneum (Hopp) |
| Superficial | Rectus lifted → below the **arcuate line** → peritoneum swept medially (Hopp) |
| Deep | Psoas lateral, ureter with peritoneum → ligate middle sacral (L5–S1) or **iliolumbar vein** (L4–5) (Hopp; AO) |
| Extension | Flank route reaches L1 → sacrum (Hopp) |

- Pre-op MRI must show the bifurcation and iliac veins (AO)

### Dangers
- **Left common iliac vein** lies flat over L5–S1 → the most fragile structure (Hopp; Campbell)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.87, 5B.88, 5B.89, 5B.90, 5B.91 · 5B.09

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|
| Left common iliac vein, IVC | Thin, stuck to the disc (Hopp) | Blunt peanut; Steinmann pin retractors (Kim) |
| Iliolumbar vein | Tethers vessels at L4–5 (AO) | Ligate **before** retracting (AO) |
| **Superior hypogastric plexus** | Left of midline over L5–S1 (Kim) | **No cautery**; sweep left → right (Kim) |
| Ureter | Crosses the iliac vessels (Hopp) | Pinch → peristalsis |
| Sympathetic chain | Medial psoas → warm ipsilateral leg (Kim) | Stay on the disc |

- Plexus injury → **retrograde ejaculation** (not impotence), up to 20% (Kim; Campbell)

PITFALL — level of the aortic bifurcation
- Hopp → on the anterior surface of **L4**; Kim → at the **L4–5 disc**
- Say → "L4 to L4–5; L5–S1 lies in the V below it → check the MRI" (AO)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "ALIF at L5–S1"
- Supine; rectus lifted, enter below the arcuate line; peritoneum + ureter medial
- **Between the iliac vessels**; ligate middle sacral vessels (L4–5 → iliolumbar vein)
- No cautery over the promontory → plexus → retrograde ejaculation · most fragile → left common iliac vein

| Levels | L5–S1 | L1 to L4–5; **not L5–S1** (Kim) |
| Risk | Presacral plexus, ileus (Hopp) | Lumbar plexus → thigh weakness up to 36% (Kim) |

- LLIF → no great-vessel mobilisation, no retrograde ejaculation (Kim)
- Flank retroperitoneal → usually **left** side (IVC harder to repair) (Campbell)

5B.10.t: Iliac Crest Bone Graft — Anterior & Posterior
5B.10.b:
### Step by step
- Rule → the crest is truly internervous: muscles attach, no nerve crosses (Hopp)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.98, 5B.99, 5B.100, 5B.101, 5B.102 · 5B.10

| Step | Anterior crest | Posterior crest |
|---|---|---|
| Uses | Tricortical graft for ACDF; most used graft (Hopp) | Posterior fusion, scoliosis (Hopp) |
| Position | Supine, sandbag under the buttock (Hopp) | Prone (Hopp) |
| Landmarks | ASIS (anterior superior iliac spine) → **iliac tubercle** (Hopp) | PSIS under the dimple (Hopp) |
| Incision | 8 cm over the tubercle, **≥3 cm behind the ASIS** (Hopp; Kim) | 8 cm oblique over the PSIS (Hopp) |
| Interval | Abdominals (segmental) / gluteus medius (superior gluteal) (Hopp) | Gluteals / paraspinals (Hopp) |
| Deep | Subperiosteal; most cancellous at the gluteus medius pillar (Campbell) | Outer table, over the posterior gluteal line (Hopp) |

- Weight-bearing grafts → oscillating saw; osteotomes microfracture (Kim)

### Dangers
- Children → split the apophysis; never carry the cut onto the ASIS (Hopp)
  [[FIG: Fig 5B.103, 5B.104, 5B.105, 5B.106 · 5B.10

| At risk | Why | Protect |
|---|---|---|

| **Superior cluneal nerves** | Cross the crest 5–7 cm lateral to the PSIS (Tubbs 2010) | Stay within 5–6 cm; Hopp allows 8 cm |
| **Superior gluteal artery** | Cut at the notch → retracts into the pelvis (Hopp) | Stay above the notch |
| Sciatic nerve | Below a line dropped from the PSIS (Hopp) | Work above it; notch intact |

- Limits → **5–6 cm** lateral to the PSIS (cluneals); above a line from the PSIS (sciatic notch)
- Superior gluteal artery cut at the notch → retracts into the pelvis

- Kim → ≥3 cm in the text, 2–3 cm in the figure; Hopp → centred on the iliac tubercle
- Say → "**≥3 cm behind the ASIS**, over the iliac tubercle"

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "iliac crest bone graft"
- Anterior → 8 cm over the iliac tubercle, **≥3 cm behind the ASIS**; risks hernia, LFCN
- Posterior → prone, 8 cm over the PSIS, outer table
- Limits → **5–6 cm** lateral to the PSIS (cluneals); above a line from the PSIS (sciatic notch)
- Superior gluteal artery cut at the notch → retracts into the pelvis
